svg.title: Architecture du U-Net ATOMOD
svg.desc: Diagramme structurel du U-Net ATOMOD avec encodeur, pont, décodeur, blocs résiduels et connexions de saut

g.ns29:text: \\begin{minipage}{8cm}\nTo extract and refine visual features at a given resolution, without changing the spatial size of the tensor.\n\\end{minipage}
\\begin{minipage}{8cm}\nMaxPool is destructive $\\rightarrow$ skip connections reinject features from the encoder into the decoder to compensate for this loss due to MaxPool\n\\end{minipage}
\\begin{flushleft}\n\\verb+ATOMOD+ takes a single simulated TEM image as input and predicts layer-by-layer (z-axis) atomic probability maps for each element:\n\\end{flushleft}
\\parbox{5cm}{\nExcellent layer-by-layer reconstruction of atomic positions from single 2D projection\n}
\\parbox{5cm}{\n$Rh$ \\& $Ir$ predictions nearly identical - TEM contrast insufficient to discriminate similar-Z elements\n}
\\parbox{10cm}{\n $\\rightarrow$ Integration of EXAFS spectra is indispensable to achieve full 3D chemical resolution. Ongoing work fuses TEM + XAS/EXAFS inputs in a multimodal encoder.\n}

g.text: N channels (Nc chemical sp. × Nz Z plans)
